html:
The Wushe incident was a rising of Seediq people at Wushe, in the mountains of central Taiwan, on 27 October 1930, against Japanese colonial rule.

Angered by forced labour and insults, warriors led by the chief Mona Rudao attacked a school sports meeting and killed about 130 Japanese. The colonial army and police struck back with artillery, aircraft and, by many accounts, poison gas, and set other indigenous groups against the rebels. Hundreds of Seediq died in battle or by suicide, among them Mona Rudao; the survivors were moved to another site, where many were later killed in a second attack.

The rising shook Japan's claim to be civilising the island and led to softer policies toward the indigenous peoples. The 2011 film Seediq Bale retold it for a new generation in Taiwan.
sum: The Wushe incident was a rising of Seediq people at Wushe, in the mountains of central Taiwan, on 27 October 1930, against Japanese colonial rule.
